newsitem.title: ANTIGUA: CRICKET-WILLIAMS, CAMPBELL CARRY WEST INDIES TO VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WILLIAMS, CAMPBELL CARRY WEST INDIES TO VICTORY.

text.p: Openers Stuart Williams and Sherwin Campbell carried West Indies to an extraordinary six-wicket victory against Sri Lanka midway through the third day of the first test on Sunday.
In a test of fluctuating fortunes, the West Indies pair belied the belief that conditions did not favour the batsmen, combining in a stand of 160 -- far and away the biggest partnership of the match.
Set 187 to win, West Indies looked set for a convincing 10-wicket victory, but in keeping with the bizarre proceedings of the previous two days the hosts then lost four wickets for just 23 runs.
It was left to Carl Hooper to hit the winning runs, a six over long-on off off-spinner Muttiah Muralitharan, ending an eventful first test match between the countries in West Indies.
Campbell, who hit a defiant half-century in West Indies' miserable first innings total of 189, struck 79 while Williams hit 83.

Williams, batting with control and command, timed the ball sweetly, as he initially dominated the first century partnership by a West Indian opening pair in 36 tests. Desmond Haynes and Phil Simmons were the last pair to do so, combining in a 122-run stand against Pakistan in 1993.
The 27-year-old right hander reached his 50 off 53 deliveries in 79 minutes with nine fours and a six, and at lunch West Indies had raced to 129 without loss.
Campbell also posted his half century before lunch and the hundred partnership came in only 98 minutes off 21.2 overs, surpassing their previous best of 85, made against New Zealand in 1995.
Williams struck 12 fours and two sixes off 118 deliveries in his 164-minute stay at the crease.
Both openers fell to Muralitharan and the unorthodox spinner snapped up the wicket of Brian Lara to finish with three for 72 to follow his first innings haul of five for 34.
After striking a four off his first delivery, Lara was caught by substitute Dulip Liyange at long-on, trying to end the game with a six.
Floyd Reifer, who batted 43 minutes for a single run, played over a full-pitched delivery from Kumara Dharmasena.
It was another remarkable achievement for Muralitharan who has successfully rebuilt a test career which looked doomed after he was no-balled for throwing in Australia in December 1995.
Sri Lanka, resuming at 151 for eight after Saturday's batting debacle in which 17 wickets fell in the day, added only one more run to their total on Sunday morning.

While Campbell claimed the batting honours, the match honours deservedly went to fast bowler Curtly Ambrose who finished with eight wickets for the match, becoming only the 12th bowler to take 300 test wickets along the way.
After the match, Ambrose, 33, praised the pitch which he said "provided assistance and encouragement for the bowler".
